_about: Student-level text for the class page. Written for 7th-8th graders from the handoff copy; takeaway lines stay verbatim in part-one.json. verse = a single verse whose text is in scripture.json; quote = an id in quotes.json. Everything else on the teacher page lives in speaker notes. moments = 'Which storyline is this?' cards; each answer matches the handoff's storyline lists or the era's speaker notes ('The storylines here').
intro: The Old Testament is the story of a house: the home God builds so He can live with us, and how He never gives up on it.

era-1.summary: God makes a home for us. We walk out. He doesn't give up.
beats: God creates the world as a beautiful home for Adam and Eve.
Adam and Eve disobey God and hide from Him.
The flood, and then the Tower of Babel.
God calls one man, Abraham, and his family: Isaac, Jacob, and Joseph.
Jacob's family moves to Egypt, where their children later become slaves.
era-1.question: Why would God ask "Where are you?" when He already knew?

moments.text: God walks in the garden with Adam and Eve
God makes them coats of skin
A promise after the Fall, a covenant after the flood, a call after Babel

era-2.summary: We can't climb up to God, so God comes down.
beats: God frees Israel from slavery in Egypt through Moses, with the ten plagues and the Passover lamb.
God gives the Law at Mount Sinai and lives among them in the Tabernacle, a tent in the middle of the camp.
Joshua leads them into the Promised Land.
The judges: Israel keeps turning away, and God keeps rescuing them.
era-2.question: Israel was rescued in one night but took forty years to change. Why is changing so much slower than being rescued?

moments.text: A tent in the middle of the camp
The judges: Israel turns away, cries out, and God rescues them, again and again

era-3.summary: Israel gets everything it asked for, and it still isn't enough.
beats: Israel asks for a king "like the nations" around them.
Three kings, forty years each: Saul, David, and Solomon.
Solomon builds the Temple, and God's glory fills it.
era-3.question: Israel got everything it asked for. Why wasn't it enough?

moments.text: God gives them the king they asked for, and doesn't leave them
The sacrifices move from the tent into the Temple

era-4.summary: God warns His people again and again, and then lets the walls fall.
beats: The kingdom splits in two: Israel in the north and Judah in the south.
God sends prophet after prophet to warn them.
Babylon conquers Judah and burns the Temple (587 BC).
era-4.question: God kept sending messengers "because he had compassion." How can a warning be an act of love?

moments.text: Prophet after prophet, warning after warning
In Babylon there is no Temple and no altar

thread-mercy.short: We fall. God forgives. Again and again.

thread-sacrifice.short: God teaches with pictures what real love costs.

thread-dwelling.short: God wants to live with us.
